research.busLimit: 4 bit, CMD6 high-speed switch active (sd_mount.c:_sd_set_mem_speed). SD_CLK_50MHz gives P1φ 66.67 MHz / 2 = 33.3 MHz, so 16.7 MB/s gross and about 15.5 MB/s net. No headroom: P1φ is fixed (FRQCR 0x1035 only sets I and P0), and the smallest divider is /2 (SDIP_SUPPORT_DIV1 is not defined). No CMD11, mount with SD_VOLT_3_3, so no UHS/1.8 V. Cards without high speed run at 16.7 MHz.
research.readPath: Per 32 KB cluster one sd_read_sect over 64 sectors: CMD13, CMD18 with automatic CMD12, DMA with 64-byte bursts (buffer aligned, always DMA thanks to the dummy cache line) and CMD13 again. Rough estimate: transfer about 2.0 ms, the card's access latency 0.1–0.5 ms (peaks 10–100 ms), commands and software 30–50 µs, cache invalidation about 20 µs. Total 2.2–2.6 ms, that is around 13 MB/s or about 70 stereo 16-bit voices.
research.scheduling: Synchronous, hardware queue depth 1, at most 128 clusters per call. The waits are busy loops with routineForSD: rendering, playbackHandler (MIDI) and UI keep running, and DMA and rendering overlap. Blocked are the slowRoutines of the main loop and further card accesses. The next command waits at most for a running render.
research.writePath: sd_write_sect with SD_WRITE_OVERWRITE, so no ACMD23. The recorder writes 32 KB via CMD25, FAT and directory sectors one by one via CMD24. The end of the busy phase is waited for in the loop with routineForSD (timeout 1–2 s): the audio keeps running, the main loop typically stalls for 3–10 ms, during the card's garbage collection up to 250/500 ms.
research.upstreamChanges: In main only cache coherence for L2 (invalidate_range_all_caches), FF_FS_TINY 0, CHMOD and renames in the scheduler. 9cd09fb7 only affects the task manager. No driver speed-up, nothing to port.

checks.claim: Bus: 4 bit, CMD6 high speed, SD_CLK_50MHz = P1φ/2 = 33.3 MHz, no /1, no UHS, without HS 16.7 MHz
checks.evidence: sd_dev_low.c:397 SD_DIV_2; sd_util.c:77 SDIP_SUPPORT_DIV1 not set; SD_DIV_1 (sdif.h:188) would give 66.7 MHz, above the HS limit of 50 MHz; peripheral_init_basic.c:97 FRQCR=0x1035; diskio.c:164 SD_VOLT_3_3; sd_mount.c:629. Whether the board can do 1.8 V cannot be checked in the code.

checks.claim: Per cluster CMD13, CMD18 with auto CMD12, DMA64, CMD13
checks.evidence: sd_read.c:203, 263-287 (SD_STOP 0x0100), 273, 345. In addition, the clock is switched on and off per read (sd_read.c:198, 385). The cluster size is the card's csize*512 and not a fixed 32 KB (audio_file_manager.cpp:86).

checks.claim: Waits are busy loops with routineForSD, slowRoutines blocked
checks.evidence: USE_TASK_MANAGER is active (CMakeLists.txt:189). sddev_int_wait (drivers/sd/sd.c:73) and the DMA wait (sd_dev_low.c:1116) call TaskManager::yield (task_scheduler.cpp:346-380). All tasks run there, including UI and slowRoutines. routineForSD runs only once per read (sd_read.c:140). Real busy waits only exist nested, with sdRoutineLock set (deluge.cpp:974-981).

checks.claim: The next command waits at most for a running render
checks.evidence: yield checks the end of the DMA only between tasks, so every task that is currently running delays the next command, e.g. OLED/UI rendering (deluge.cpp:597, 620).

diskio.c:256 passes 0x0001 = SD_WRITE_OVERWRITE (sdif.h:151); the ACMD23 path exists (sd_write.c:211-214); SD_TIMEOUT_RESP 1000 (sd.h:262); DMA at least 2 s (sd_dev_low.c:1112). The risk is overstated: pre-erase only affects blocks that are overwritten anyway.
git diff release_1_2_1..main: in sd_read.c and sd_write.c only invalidate_range_all_caches for L2 (a2f8bc51, 260ac76c). 1.2.1 already has the flush before writing (sd_write.c:164).

checks.claim: One CMD18 over following clusters brings 10–20%
checks.evidence: Not proven: the cluster buffers are not contiguous in RAM, and the queue is sorted by priority across many voices. Adjacent sectors are rare in it. The gain is unknown.
This is only partly true: only values above 7 ms are printed, and only with debug output (audio_file_manager.cpp:975, 1066-1071). For typical values the threshold must be lowered.

verdict.missed: Streaming bypasses FatFs, because sdAddress is precomputed (audio_file_manager.cpp:1063). FASTSEEK and exFAT are therefore irrelevant for playback. The real lever for latency is the scheduling: the latency between the end of the DMA and the next command depends on how long the other tasks take. Worth checking would be allowing only short tasks during an SD wait. This can be measured with REPORT_AWAY_TIME and a lower REPORT_LOAD_TIME threshold.
